nodes.title: Adopt Apple Memory Integrity Enforcement (MIE) for macOS builds
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Apple shipped a new feature in Tahoe called Memory Integrity Enforcement (MIE).
This (much) better protects against buffer overflow attacks.
For any non-Apple applications, this should be enabled during compilation time. (opt-in)
I think this would be an amazing benefit for all electron users if those applications (Slack, ...) could benefit from the same protections.

How to enable: Xcode -> Enhanced Security -> Enable Hardware Memory Tagging

### Proposed Solution

Add to Clang for macOS arm64 builds: `-fsanitize=memtag`

### Alternatives Considered

N/A

### Additional Information

More information: https://security.apple.com/blog/memory-integrity-enforcement/

nodes.title: Incorrect signal variable reference causes wrong error detection in nan-spec-runner.js
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 25.04

### What arch are you using?

x86_64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test



**The Problem**
On [Line 115 - status destructure](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L115)  the install spawn only destructures status but not signal .
Then on [Line 122 - signal check](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L122) , the code checks signal which refers to the [Line 103 - build process signal](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f784ea6f4f98a12208c9dc42d7e437280e285a06/script/nan-spec-runner.js#L103)  not the install process signal.



**Expected Behavior(2 cases  here )**

_Scenario 1_: Install process killed by signal (e.g: SIGTERM, SIGINT)
when: User presses Ctrl+C during yarn install, or CI timeout kills the process

Expected:

1. Install process exits with _installSatus=null_  and   ``` installSignal = 'SIGTERM' ```
2. Error check detects the signal termination
3. Script exits with error message: "Failed to install nan node_modules"
4. Exit code reflects the signal termination

_Scenario 2_: Build killed but install succeeds

when: Build process was terminated by signal but install completes successfully

Expected:

1. Build process fails and script exits (already handled correctly) 
2. If build somehow continues, install process completes with installStatus=0, ``` installSignal = null ```
3. Install validation passes
4. Script continues to next step

### Actual Behavior

Scenario 1: Install process killed by signal
What actually happens:

1. Install process exits with _installSatus=null_  and signal = 'SIGTERM'
2. Error check evaluates: ``` if (installStatus !== 0 || signal != null) ```
3. signal refers to the build signal from line 103, which is null (build succeeded)
4. Check fails to detect the install termination 
5. Script continues as if install succeeded, leading to downstream failures

Scenario 2: Build killed but install succeeds
What actually happens:


1. Build fails with signal (correctly exits early - this scenario won't happen)
2. But hypothetically, if build signal was set and install succeeded:
     -   Check evaluates: ```  if (0 !== 0 || 'SIGTERM' != null) ```
     -   Incorrectly reports install failure 
     -   Exits with wrong error message

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

nodes.title: don't crash without `spellcheck::kWinDelaySpellcheckServiceInit`
nodes.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I am a [maintainer](https://github.com/orgs/electron/people) of the Electron project. (If not, please create a [different issue type](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/).)

### Description

The `spellcheck::kWinDelaySpellcheckServiceInit` feature has been [removed upstream](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7012087) but we've been using it since c2d7164 (#38248) to fix a crash originally described in 97b353a (#34993):

> Delaying spell check initialization is causing specs for 'custom dictionary word list API' to fail in Electron.

I tried removing the flag locally in the Oct 21 2025 roll and confirmed the crash is still happening, so I reverted the upstream removal in https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48618 which adds a ~750 line patch. We should fix the crash and remove this patch.

nodes.title: Windows: Open Folder dialog is not accessible with `'multiSelections', 'openDirectory', 'createDirectory'`
Windows Native Print Dialog fails to appear in the foreground if triggered while already open in the background
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.2.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The existing native print dialog should be brought to the foreground and receive focus, allowing the user to interact with it.

### Actual Behavior

The print dialog remains in the background, out of view. The user cannot see the dialog appear on the screen, giving the impression that the print button is broken or unresponsive. A new dialog is not created (which is correct behavior for modal dialogs), but the existing one is not focused.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When a user triggers the native print dialog in an Electron application (using either window.print() in the renderer or mainWindow.webContents.print() in the main process), if the dialog is dismissed or moved to the background, triggering the print command again does not bring the existing dialog to the foreground. The dialog remains hidden behind the main Electron application window or other running applications.
This behavior prevents users from interacting with the print dialog a second time without manually searching for it in their OS taskbar/dock.

nodes.title: Fix logical bug in checksums environment variable handling in npm/install.js
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.0.0 and above 

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 25.04

### What arch are you using?

x86_64 



### Expected Behavior

This makes the intent clearer:  
   if either environment variable is truthy, skip local checksums



``` checksums: (process.env.electron_use_remote_checksums || process.env.npm_config_electron_use_remote_checksums) ? undefined : require('./checksums.json'), ```



### Actual Behavior

There is a logical bug in   _install.js_   line 47  where the environment variable check for _electron_use_remotechecksums_     doesn't work correctly due to operator precedence 





The ternary operator (?:) has lower precedence than the nullish coalescing operator (??), so the code is evaluated as:




``` checksums: (process.env.electron_use_remote_checksums ?? process.env.npm_config_electron_use_remote_checksums) ? undefined : require('./checksums.json') ```


- If either variable is set to a truthy value, it uses remote checksums 
- But the logic is confusing and not what was likely intended

nodes.title: BrowserWindow.getBounds() includes transparent space taken up by shadows on Wayland
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`BrowserWindow.getBounds()` should return the bounds of the visible, physical window (contentBounds + titlebar). It should not include the transparent area which surrounds the window to support shadows.
### Actual Behavior

This window will report bounds of 800x600 immediately after creation, but soon reports larger bounds of 844x822, even though the visible window is still 800x600.

```  
const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js')
    }
  })

  // Will be 844x822
  setTimeout(() => {
    console.log("Main window bounds after 1s:", mainWindow.getBounds());
  }, 1000);
```
The larger bounds  are returned because the window is surrounded by a transparent client-drawn frame which paints shadows + the outer part of resize handle hit targets, but this is an implementation detail which is not relevant to the app.

This is an issue because if an app implements window bounds saving/restoration, windows will grow a little more each time they are created. (A bug for that specific manifestation of this issue may have been filed already.)

## Isn't this what BrowserWindow.getContentBounds() is for?

No. `BrowserWindow.getContentBounds()` returns the web content bounds only, i.e. it subtracts the titlebar.  An 800x600 window has these sets of bounds when drawn with CSD (ClientFrameViewLinux):

- Total bounds including transparent shadow region: 844x644
- Window bounds (visible window frame): 800x600
- Content bounds: 800x532

That second value is the one which needs to be consistently respected by `BrowserWindow.getBounds()`, since it is supposed to be the same measurement as the value which is set on window creation. The total CSD bounds including external decorations do not need to be accessible from the JS layer.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/7487efc43b208a3624ba464cb156860d

### Additional Information

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`BrowserWindow.getBounds()` should show the bounds of the visible, physical window (contentBounds + titlebar). It should not include the transparent area which surrounds the window to support shadows + resize handle hit targets.

### Actual Behavior

This window will report bounds of 800x600 immediately after creation, but soon reports larger bounds of 844x822, even though the visible window is still 800x600.

```  
const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js')
    }
  })

  // Will be 844x822
  setTimeout(() => {
    console.log("Main window bounds after 1s:", mainWindow.getBounds());
  }, 1000);
```
The larger bounds  are given because the window is surrounded by a transparent client-drawn frame to support shadows + hit targets, but this is an implementation detail. This is an issue because if an app implements window bounds saving/restoration, windows will grow a little more each time they are created. (This bug may have been filed already.)

## Isn't this what BrowserWindow.getContentBounds() is for?

No. `BrowserWindow.getContentBounds()` returns the web content bounds only, i.e. it subtracts the titlebar. For an 800x600 window, the bounds are:

- Total absolute bounds including transparent region; 844x822
- Window bounds: 800x600
- Client bounds: 800x532

That second value is the one which needs to be consistently respected by `BrowserWindow.getBounds()`, since it is related to the one which is set (correctly) on window creation. The total bounds including external decorations aren't relevant to app creators or users.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/7487efc43b208a3624ba464cb156860d

### Additional Information

Related to: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48588.

nodes.title: Windows shrink the first time they lose focus on Wayland
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

An 800x600 window should be able to keep consistent dimensions after creation, including when it loses focus. 

### Actual Behavior

An 800x600 window goes on a journey after you create it, first starting at 800x600 absolute bounds (which is incorrect: see #48589), then growing to its proper size after creation and then shrinking to about 785x580 if you click out of it to lose focus.

Logs from the Fiddle:

```
Main window bounds at creation: { x: 645, y: 172, width: 800, height: 600 }
Main window bounds after 1s: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 844, height: 644 }
Main window bounds after blur (assuming you manually de-focused it): { x: 0, y: 0, width: 822, height: 625 }
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mitchchn/7487efc43b208a3624ba464cb156860d

### Additional Information

Some context to help diagnose the root cause: on Wayland (and in GNOME specifically), Electron draws all window decorations using CSD, including titlebars, borderes, and shadows.

This means that an 800x600 BrowserWindow actually sits inside a larger 844x644 transparent frame into which the active shadows are drawn. When the window goes inactive, the shadows are drawn thinner, so the transparent frame shrinks. This incorrectly causes the client area of the window to shrink as well. (But for some reason everything works fine after the first time the window loses focus on subsequent focus cycles.)

nodes.title: App crashed with white screen while using Claude for product selection
nodes.body:
I was using Claude to help me pick a DisplayPort splitter for my new Windows machine when the app suddenly crashed. The window turned into a white screen and just kept spinning forever.

I was in the middle of having Claude help me with product selection on Amazon when this happened. The app became completely unresponsive - just a white screen with a loading spinner that never completed.

**Success looks like:**
- [ ] App doesn't crash during normal usage
- [ ] If something goes wrong, the app recovers gracefully instead of showing an infinite white screen
- [ ] Loading states have timeouts and proper error handling

nodes.title: Double Shift keyboard shortcut not responding reliably
nodes.body:
I was working with Claude to help me pick a DisplayPort splitter for my new Windows machine when I noticed the double shift keyboard shortcut wasn't responding. I had to press double shift multiple times before it would finally register and work. I was doing it the exact same way every single time, but it just wouldn't pick it up for some reason.

After several attempts of pressing double shift with no response, it would randomly work on one of the attempts. There doesn't seem to be a pattern to when it works versus when it doesn't - it's intermittent.

This makes the keyboard shortcut unreliable for triggering actions in the application.

**Success looks like:**
- [ ] Double shift keyboard shortcut reliably triggers on every attempt
- [ ] No need to press it multiple times before it registers

### Problem Description

this page is out of date https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/tutorial/native-code-and-electron-cpp-linux.md
It uses and advocates for GTK 3

> We specifically use GTK3 because that's what Chromium (and by extension, Electron) uses internally. Using GTK4 would cause runtime conflicts since both GTK3 and GTK4 would be loaded in the same process. If and when Chromium upgrades to GTK4, you will likely be able to easily upgrade your native code to GTK4, too.

Chromium supports GTK4, and support for it can be enabled at runtime using the --gtk-version=4 command-line flag. This is particularly useful for input methods (IME) under Wayland and can be used to enable GTK4 features



### Proposed Solution

Provide guidance for working with GTK4 - AFAIK, this is a precursor step for Wayland support https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/39732

Tauri ? 
Qt https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/wayland-and-qt.html

nodes.title: Provide official TypeScript types for Chromium-specific Web APIs (e.g., navigator.bluetooth)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The TypeScript team's policy mandates that Web API types only get included after being implemented in at least two browser engines. However, this constraint doesn't align with Electron's reality where we have a single Chrome-based runtime.

A concrete example is `navigator.bluetooth` - while functionally available in Electron, it triggers TypeScript type errors due to its exclusion from the official lib.d.ts definitions.

### Proposed Solution

It would be beneficial to have a type definition such as `import { type webapi } from "electron"` to enable `bluetooth` injection into the `navigator` object. This type should be automatically maintained to align with the Chrome versions supported by Electron.

### Alternatives Considered

write by developer self
```ts
declare global {
    interface navigator {
        bluetooth: ...
    }
}
```

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Add support for LanguageDetector and Translator APIs
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

In Electron at the moment, the [`LanguageDetector`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/language-detection) and [`Translator`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/translator-api) APIs appear to be present, but if called the language detector rejects with `UnknownError: Model not available`, and the `Translator` APIs never resolve the promise.

### Proposed Solution

Are the models for these in Chrome open/available for use in Electron? If so, it would be great if these could be made available. Given they're downloaded on demand in Chrome, I can see that would introduce a complication; being able to self-host the downloads would be good, but fine if they're just always downloaded from Google.

### Alternatives Considered

On Mac we could add a custom integration with the system translate APIs, but a built-in solution would be preferable due to easier maintenance and cross-platform compatibility. We could call out to an external service, but especially for language detection isn't suitable for our purposes; we want it to happen on device.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.body:

### Problem Description

Right now, `webContents` need to be closed manually. See [here](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/676406c9e6664ad94c818475249442100b068bf7/docs/api/base-window.md#resource-management).

### Proposed Solution

Close `webContents` automatically when they are no longer referenced in any form.

### Alternatives Considered

Continue having to close them manually.

### Additional Information

Docs PR that documented having to close the `webContents`: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/43610

Fiddle gist to see that calling `close` is necessary: https://gist.github.com/nikwen/dacdd75daff9eb17af01fd528cdbdefc

This will be a breaking change.
